## Dimorphos’s Orbit Continued to Change After DART

Dimorphos, the smaller asteroid orbiting Didymos, took 11 hours and 55 minutes to complete an orbit before DART’s impact. Its orbital period was shorter immediately after the impact, then continued to shorten over the following weeks. During that period, Dimorphos also lost more rocky material to space.

The period eventually settled at about 11 hours and 22 minutes—roughly 33 minutes shorter than before the impact. Dimorphos’s orbit was also no longer circular. The orbital change, in other words, continued beyond the immediate aftermath of DART.
